title: Property & Lease Profile
intro: Everything this project actually knows about the asset, separated into what the owner stated and what an official record can confirm. The owner's address, parcel number (APN), rent roll, purchase basis and operating statements were never supplied and are deliberately not reconstructed here — doing so would both fabricate data and defeat the privacy requirement.

rows.note: Internal placeholder. No address, APN, latitude/longitude or assessor link is stored in this repository.
Personal identifiers removed at intake.
Owner-stated. No public record corroborates this; the lease itself was not provided.
Owner-stated. Whether the tenant of record is a franchisee or the corporate entity is NOT known and is a material unknown (see R-02).
No further geographic precision is stored. All market data in this project is therefore measured at City of Los Angeles, County of Los Angeles or LA–Long Beach–Anaheim MSA level.
Owner-stated range, not verified against the lease document.
Derived arithmetic from PR-06. Three cases are modelled rather than one point estimate.
Unknown. This is the single most important missing document term: it determines whether the owner or the tenant controls the post-2030 outcome.
Not provided; withheld for privacy. The model is therefore normalised to $1.00 of NOI.

rows.metric: Building area, land area, parking ratio, drive-thru
rows.note: Not provided. Drive-thru presence materially changes re-leasing prospects for a QSR box and is the first item to confirm.

rows.metric: Zoning, general plan designation, entitlement upside
rows.note: Requires the parcel number to query ZIMAS (City of LA). Not attempted, by design.

rows.metric: Assessed value, base-year value, annual property tax
rows.note: Requires the APN to query the Los Angeles County Assessor. Not attempted, by design.

rows.metric: Current NOI, purchase price, adjusted basis
rows.note: Not provided. Without adjusted basis no after-tax comparison can be computed; the model reports pre-tax wealth and treats tax as a documented overlay (see V-07 to V-10).

rows.metric: Jack in the Box system units at 2026-07-05
rows.note: 149 company-operated + 1,966 franchised.

rows.metric: Share of system that is franchised
rows.note: 1,966 franchised ÷ 2,115 total. Makes it likely, but not certain, that PARCEL-01's tenant is a franchisee rather than the corporate parent.

rows.metric: Jack in the Box same-store sales, Q3 FY2026
rows.note: Franchise same-store sales (1.2%), company (0.9%). An improvement from (7.1%) a year earlier.

rows.metric: Jack in the Box same-store sales, FY2025
rows.note: Q4 FY2025 alone was (7.4%).
38 of the 47 Q4 closures were part of the 'JACK on Track' block-closure programme.
Guidance issued with Q4 FY2025 results: restaurant count of 2,050–2,100, 'approximately 50 to 100 closures, most of which will be franchise restaurants'.

rows.metric: Franchised restaurant average unit volume, FY2025
rows.note: Down from $1,949,000 in FY2024. Useful for stress-testing whether the store can carry market rent.
The brand is now a single-concept operator, which concentrates franchisee and landlord exposure on the Jack in the Box banner.

rows.display: Mark King, Interim CEO (from 2026); refinancing completed
rows.note: Leadership turnover at the franchisor is a second-order but real signal for renewal decisions.

rows.metric: Franchisor sells owned real estate to franchisees
rows.note: Trade press reported a plan to sell land/building at roughly 170 franchised sites as part of the 2025 'JACK on Track' programme. This could not be confirmed in the SEC exhibit retrieved for this project, so it is flagged rather than asserted.
